description: Sichuan Kung Pao Chicken is a fiery and flavorful stir-fry, renowned for its complex balance of spicy, sweet, sour, and savory notes. Cubes of tender chicken are wok-tossed with crunchy peanuts, aromatic dried chilies, and the signature tingling sensation of Sichuan peppercorns. This iconic dish offers an exhilarating culinary journey for adventurous palates, delivering an authentic taste of Sichuan cuisine right to your home.

ingredients.notes: cut into 1-inch pieces, seeds removed if less heat desired

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, combine the cubed chicken with 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, and 1.5 tablespoons cornstarch. Mix well until the chicken is evenly coated. Set aside to marinate for at least 15 minutes while you prepare other ingredients.

instructions.title: Prepare the Kung Pao Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons light soy sauce, 1 teaspoon dark soy sauce, 2 tablespoons Chinese black vinegar, 2 tablespoons sugar, 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, 1 teaspoon cornstarch, and 2 tablespoons water or chicken broth until the sugar is dissolved and the sauce is smooth. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of peanut or vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer and cook for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside, leaving any residual oil in the wok.

instructions.title: Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium-high. Add the dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns to the wok and stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant and slightly darkened. Be careful not to burn them. Add the minced garlic, minced ginger, and the white parts of the green onions. Stir-fry for another 15-30 seconds until aromatic.

instructions.title: Combine and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the seared chicken to the wok. Give the prepared Kung Pao sauce a quick stir to re-mix the cornstarch, then pour it over the chicken and aromatics. Stir quickly to coat everything evenly. The sauce will thicken rapidly.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Add the roasted peanuts and the green parts of the green onions to the wok. Toss everything together for another 30 seconds to heat through. Remove from heat immediately. Serve hot with steamed white rice.

tips: For authentic Sichuan flavor, do not skip the Sichuan peppercorns; they provide the unique 'ma la' tingling sensation. Toast them lightly before use to enhance their aroma.
Ensure your wok is very hot before adding ingredients for stir-frying. This helps create a smoky 'wok hei' flavor and prevents the chicken from steaming.
Prep all your ingredients, especially the sauce, before you start cooking. Stir-frying is a fast process, and you won't have time to chop or measure once the heat is on.
